# nylla

[![Nylla](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/nylla@latest/docs/assets/nylla-og.jpeg)](https://nylla.dev/)

Point your AI coding tools at **[Nylla](https://nylla.dev/)**, the hosted AI API that gives you many
models behind one API key. `nylla` writes the base URL, model and key into each tool's own
configuration; it does not run or proxy anything.

## Quick start

You need Node.js 24.15 or later (or 26 or later), a Nylla account and API key, and at least one
supported tool. The Nylla key is not your ChatGPT, Claude or Google key.

```bash
npx nylla init
# or install it: npm install -g nylla && nylla init
```

Setup asks for your language (English or Brazilian Portuguese) and your key, in a masked prompt. It
lets you pick tools and models and shows every change before writing it. Afterwards, open a new
terminal, restart your tools and run `nylla status`.

## Supported tools

| Tool | ID | Setup |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Claude Code | `claude-code` | Automatic; Shortcut `ny-claude` by default |
| Codex CLI | `codex` | Automatic; Shortcut `ny-codex` by default |
| OpenCode | `opencode` | Automatic |
| Hermes Agent | `hermes` | Automatic |
| Pi | `pi` | Automatic |
| OpenClaw | `openclaw` | Automatic; not yet checked in running installs |
| Copilot VS Code | `vscode` | Automatic; not yet checked in running installs |
| Cursor | `cursor` | Guided steps; chat and agent only, not Tab or inline edit |

**Shortcut** mode leaves `claude` and `codex` as they are and adds `ny-claude` and `ny-codex` (with a
global install; otherwise `npx nylla shortcut claude-code`). **Override** (`--mode override`) points
the normal commands at Nylla instead, after asking.

## Commands

Without a global install, put `npx` in front.

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `nylla init` | Set up or change your tools |
| `nylla status` | Check the Nylla API and what each tool has configured |
| `nylla list` | Supported tools installed here; `--all` for every supported tool |
| `nylla models` | Models available through Nylla |
| `nylla apply <id>` | Configure one tool |
| `nylla remove <id>` | Remove Nylla's configuration from one tool; `--all` for every tool |
| `nylla doctor` | Send small real requests to diagnose the connection (counts toward usage) |
| `nylla run <command>` | Run a command with the Nylla variables set, writing nothing |
| `nylla snippet <target>` | Print the setup for a tool, an SDK, `devcontainer`, `github-actions` or `docker` |
| `nylla env` | Add the Nylla variables to your shell profile; `--print` or `--remove` |
| `nylla uninstall` | Undo everything: tool settings, shell block and saved key |

Common flags: `--dry-run` shows the changes and writes nothing, `--yes` skips prompts, `--model <id>`
pins a model, `--output json` prints machine-readable output. In scripts and CI, set `NYLLA_API_KEY`
instead of saving a key.

```bash
nylla apply claude-code --dry-run
```

## Your key and files

- The key goes in the OS keychain (Secret Service on Linux). It falls back to a private file only
  when there is no keychain, and never on CI or Windows.
- Each tool gets the key with no step of yours: in its own configuration file (private to you), or
  from `ny-claude` and `ny-codex` when they start. Codex on Override reads `NYLLA_API_KEY`, so
  `nylla init` and `nylla apply` export it in your shell profile; open a new terminal after.
- Each configuration file is backed up before it changes. Backups can still hold the old
  credentials, so keep them out of repositories.
- Debug logs and traces stay on this machine: **Settings → Open logs folder** in the menu.

## If something does not work

- **Missing or rejected key:** run `nylla init`, or check the key in your Nylla account.
- **A tool still uses its old settings:** open a new terminal, restart the tool and run
  `nylla status`. In Shortcut mode, start it with `ny-claude` or `ny-codex`.
- **Connection errors:** run `nylla doctor`. The Nylla API is at `https://api.nylla.dev`.
- **Behind a proxy:** set `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1` along with `HTTPS_PROXY` or `HTTP_PROXY`.

## Remove it

```bash
nylla uninstall
npm uninstall -g nylla
```

For Cursor, follow **Your action** in the uninstall report, then restart your tools.
